Guides / Battle & team / Battles & stats

Battles & stats

How auto battles run: stats, IVs, natures, damage, status and the Catcher.

StatsIVs and naturesDamageStatusTerrainsDitto: Transform and ImposterMovesWhen both sides fall

Battles are one-on-one: your lead fights, your bench helps (see Roles), and when the lead faints the next steps in. Wild battles end after 60 turns (it wanders off), bosses after 120, Gyms after 200.

Stats

Stats follow the main games: base stats, IVs (0–31) and a nature, no EVs. HP = ⌊(2 × base + IV) × level ÷ 100⌋ + level + 10; other stats = (⌊(2 × base + IV) × level ÷ 100⌋ + 5) × nature. Then Tallgrass multiplies everything by power:

SourceStats
RarityCommon ×1, Uncommon ×1.05, Rare ×1.15, Legendary ×1.35
Shiny / Alpha / Perfect IVs×1.1 / ×1.2 / ×1.1
Void / Prismatic / both×1.2 / ×1.3 / ×1.4 (and +0.4 / +0.6 / +0.7 × level HP)
Power-ups+3% per level, up to +30%
DPS role+15% Attack and Sp. Atk
Squad bodyHP ×1.25, Attack and Sp. Atk ×1.05
Team bonusBalanced squad ×1.1, a Prismatic in the party ×1.1
Held stat itemsChoice items +30%, Assault Vest +30% Sp. Def, Eviolite +40% defences…

A calculator runs in the live wiki. Open this page in the live wiki to use it.

IVs and natures

IVs are 0–31 for each stat, fixed by the Pokémon's personality. The card shows their average as a %: perfect 100%, great 80%+, good 55%+. Perfect-IV Pokémon have all six at 31. Natures raise one stat ×1.1 and lower another ×0.9 (5 are neutral). On the PC card and the Hunt cards the raised stat shows in green with a "+" and the lowered one in red with a "−" ("+Atk −SpA" next to the nature's name).

Damage

  • The main games' formula: level, power, Attack vs Defense, a random 85–100% roll, STAB ×1.5, weather, critical hits ×1.5 (base 1 in 24).
  • Type matchups are amplified: super effective ×1.5 more, resisted ×0.6 (see Types).
  • Squad Leader skills and Synergies add their boosts on top (see Squads).
  • Abilities, burns (physical ×0.5), stat stages, Protect, two-turn moves, multi-hit, drain and recoil work like the games. Rollout, Outrage, Thrash and Uproar lock in for several turns.

Status

Burn, paralysis, poison, bad poison, sleep (1–3 turns) and freeze work like the main games. For catching, asleep / frozen = ×2.5, any other status ×1.5.

Terrains

Some abilities lay a terrain for 5 turns when their Pokémon comes in. Terrains only touch Pokémon on the ground (not Flying types, Levitate or anything up in the sky), work in every battle except raids, and show as a tag under the weather on the battle screen.

TerrainSet byEffect
Electric TerrainElectric Surge, Hadron EngineElectric moves from grounded users +30%. Grounded Pokémon can't fall asleep.
Grassy TerrainGrassy Surge, Seed Sower (when hit)Grass moves from grounded users +30%. Grounded Pokémon heal 1/16 of their HP each turn. Earthquake, Bulldoze and Magnitude hit grounded targets half as hard.
Psychic TerrainPsychic SurgePsychic moves from grounded users +30%. Priority moves can't hit grounded targets.
Misty TerrainMisty SurgeDragon moves hit grounded targets half as hard. Grounded Pokémon can't get a status or be confused.
  • Hadron Engine: sets Electric Terrain, and its Sp. Atk is ×4/3 on it.
  • Quark Drive: on Electric Terrain its best stat is ×1.3 (×1.5 if that's Speed).
  • Surge Surfer: doubles its Speed on Electric Terrain.
  • Rising Voltage doubles in power on Electric Terrain (grounded target); Expanding Force is ×1.5 on Psychic Terrain (grounded user).

Ditto: Transform and Imposter

Ditto knows Transform: it becomes a copy of the foe (its look, types, stats but not HP, stat changes, moves with 5 PP each, and ability). A Ditto with Imposter copies the foe the moment it comes in. It turns back into Ditto when it leaves the field. In raids Ditto fights as before.

Moves

Every Pokémon auto-picks its 4 strongest damaging moves from what it has learned (repeat types count a little less, for coverage). Pin moves to keep them. See Moves & the Move Tutor.

When both sides fall

If the foe and your last Pokémon faint on the same turn, the battle still counts as a win, and your whole party goes to the Pokémon Center to rest (in hunts, bosses and Gyms).
